Here is the report on the winners in the Film categories for the 82nd Golden Globes, held on January 5, 2025.

### **82nd Golden Globe Awards – Film Winners Report**
**Date:** January 5, 2025
**Location:** Beverly Hilton Hotel, Beverly Hills, California
**Host:** Nikki Glaser

#### **Best Motion Picture**
*   **Drama:** ***The Brutalist*** (Nominees: *A Complete Unknown*, *Conclave*, *Dune: Part Two*, *Nickel Boys*, *September 5*)
*   **Musical or Comedy:** ***Emilia Pérez*** (Nominees: *Anora*, *Challengers*, *A Real Pain*, *The Substance*, *Wicked*)
*   **Animated:** ***Flow*** (Nominees: *Inside Out 2*, *Memoir of a Snail*, *Moana 2*, *Wallace & Gromit: Vengeance Most Fowl*, *The Wild Robot*)
*   **Non-English Language:** ***Emilia Pérez*** (France) (Nominees: *All We Imagine as Light* [India], *The Girl with the Needle* [Denmark], *I'm Still Here* [Brazil], *The Seed of the Sacred Fig* [Germany], *Vermiglio* [Italy])

#### **Best Actor in a Motion Picture**
*   **Drama:** **Adrien Brody** (*The Brutalist*) as László Tóth
    *   Nominees: Timothée Chalamet (*A Complete Unknown*), Daniel Craig (*Queer*), Colman Domingo (*Sing Sing*), Ralph Fiennes (*Conclave*), Sebastian Stan (*The Apprentice*)
*   **Musical or Comedy:** **Sebastian Stan** (*A Different Man*) as Edward Lemuel / Guy Moratz
    *   Nominees: Jesse Eisenberg (*A Real Pain*), Hugh Grant (*Heretic*), Gabriel LaBelle (*Saturday Night*), Jesse Plemons (*Kinds of Kindness*), Glen Powell (*Hit Man*)

#### **Best Actress in a Motion Picture**
*   **Drama:** **Fernanda Torres** (*I'm Still Here*) as Eunice Paiva
    *   Nominees: Pamela Anderson (*The Last Showgirl*), Angelina Jolie (*Maria*), Nicole Kidman (*Babygirl*), Tilda Swinton (*The Room Next Door*), Kate Winslet (*Lee*)
*   **Musical or Comedy:** **Demi Moore** (*The Substance*) as Elisabeth Sparkle
    *   Nominees: Amy Adams (*Nightbitch*), Cynthia Erivo (*Wicked*), Karla Sofía Gascón (*Emilia Pérez*), Mikey Madison (*Anora*), Zendaya (*Challengers*)

#### **Best Supporting Actor in a Motion Picture**
*   **Overall:** **Kieran Culkin** (*A Real Pain*) as Benji Kaplan
    *   Nominees: Yura Borisov (*Anora*), Edward Norton (*A Complete Unknown*), Guy Pearce (*The Brutalist*), Jeremy Strong (*The Apprentice*), Denzel Washington (*Gladiator II*)

#### **Best Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture**
*   **Overall:** **Zoe Saldaña** (*Emilia Pérez*) as Rita Mora Castro
    *   Nominees: Selena Gomez (*Emilia Pérez*), Ariana Grande (*Wicked*), Felicity Jones (*The Brutalist*), Margaret Qualley (*The Substance*), Isabella Rossellini (*Conclave*)

#### **Best Director**
*   **Overall:** **Brady Corbet** (*The Brutalist*)
    *   Nominees: Jacques Audiard (*Emilia Pérez*), Sean Baker (*Anora*), Edward Berger (*Conclave*), Coralie Fargeat (*The Substance*), Payal Kapadia (*All We Imagine as Light*)

#### **Best Screenplay**
*   **Overall:** **Peter Straughan** (*Conclave*)
    *   Nominees: Jacques Audiard (*Emilia Pérez*), Sean Baker (*Anora*), Brady Corbet and Mona Fastvold (*The Brutalist*), Jesse Eisenberg (*A Real Pain*), Coralie Fargeat (*The Substance*)

#### **Best Original Score**
*   **Overall:** **Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross** (*Challengers*)
    *   Nominees: Volker Bertelmann (*Conclave*), Daniel Blumberg (*The Brutalist*), Kris Bowers (*The Wild Robot*), Clément Ducol and Camille (*Emilia Pérez*), Hans Zimmer (*Dune: Part Two*)

#### **Best Original Song**
*   **Overall:** "**El Mal**" by Clément Ducol, Camille, and Jacques Audiard from *Emilia Pérez*
    *   Nominees: "Beautiful That Way" (*The Last Showgirl*), "Compress / Repress" (*Challengers*), "Forbidden Road" (*Better Man*), "Kiss the Sky" (*The Wild Robot*), "Mi camino" (*Emilia Pérez*)

#### **Cinematic and Box Office Achievement**
*   **Winner:** ***Wicked*** (2024 film)
    *   Nominees: *Alien: Romulus*, *Beetlejuice Beetlejuice*, *Deadpool & Wolverine*, *Gladiator II*, *Inside Out 2*, *Twisters*, *The Wild Robot*

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)

# Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models

Hugo Abonizio* Rodrigo Nogueira* Ramon Pires* Affiliation: Maritaca AI

Technical Report

∗Equal contribution

###### Abstract

We introduce Sabiá-2, a family of large language models trained on Portuguese texts. The models are evaluated on a diverse range of exams, including entry-level tests for Brazilian universities, professional certification exams, and graduate-level exams for various disciplines such as accounting, economics, engineering, law and medicine. Our results reveal that our best model so far, Sabiá-2 Medium, matches or surpasses GPT-4’s performance in 23 out of 64 exams and outperforms GPT-3.5 in 58 out of 64 exams. Notably, specialization has a significant impact on a model’s performance without the need to increase its size, allowing us to offer Sabiá-2 Medium at a price per token that is 10 times cheaper than GPT-4. Finally, we identified that math and coding are key abilities that need improvement.

## 1 Introduction

Specialization has shown to be a highly effective strategy for improving the performance of models without the need to increase their parameter count and, consequently, the inference cost. This approach, when contrasted with general-purpose models, offers significant improvements in efficiency and accuracy. The move towards domain-specific specialization in areas such as code [[17](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib17 "")], mathematics [[4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib4 ""), [9](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib9 "")], finance [[21](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib21 "")], and medicine [[7](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib7 ""), [20](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib20 "")] highlights the broad applicability and success of this strategy across diverse fields. Furthermore, in the realm of language specialization, models in Portuguese [[15](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib15 ""), [8](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib8 ""), [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib6 ""), [11](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib11 "")], Thai [[14](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib14 "")], Persian [[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib1 "")], Arabic [[18](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib18 "")], Traditional Chinese [[10](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib10 "")], and Southeast Asian languages [[12](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib12 "")] exemplify this recent trend.

In this work, we introduce Sabiá-2, a family of LLMs specially trained on Portuguese texts.11 1 Due to the current competitive landscape, we do not reveal our training methodology and the architecture of the models. We evaluate Sabiá-2 and other proprietary and open-source models on a diverse set of Brazilian benchmarks, including academic and professional exams, and multi-turn conversations with cultural characteristics. It is important to note that no specific training was conducted for the exams under investigation.

Sabiá-2 Medium showcases strong in-domain results. Compared with other proprietary LLMs, Sabiá-2 Medium performs on par or better than GPT-3.5 Turbo and Gemini 1.0 Pro in 96.9% of the exams. It also outperforms Mistral large, which is 8 times more expensive, in 76.6% of the exams.
At present, the MariTalk [[2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib2 "")] assistant uses Sabiá-2 Medium.

The report is organized as follows: Section [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S2 "2 Academic and Professional Benchmarks ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") describes the academic and professional benchmarks, and Section [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3 "3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") introduces the Brazilian multi-turn conversation benchmark.
Section [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4 "4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") outlines the capabilities of the Sabiá models and other open-source and proprietary models on exams benchmarks.
Section [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S5 "5 Capabilities on Conversations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents the results of our analysis of the abilities of the models in following instructions and multi-turn conversations majorly with contents related to Brazilian culture.
Section [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S6 "6 Limitations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") discusses the limitations of the models, and Section [7](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S7 "7 Conclusion ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") offers concluding remarks and suggests avenues for future research.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_the_National_Student_Performance_Exam.png)Figure 1: Results of Sabiá-2, GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 Turbo on Enade 2022 and 2023 exams, ordered from low to high based on Sabiá-2 performance. Sabiá-2 outperforms GPT-3.5 Turbo on most exams, except Control and Automation Engineering, and Medicine. The lowest accuracies were achieved in domains related to engineering and economics. However, GPT-4 Turbo demonstrates consistent high accuracy across the spectrum.

## 2 Academic and Professional Benchmarks

Brazil has a strong tradition on public academic assessment that plays an important role in the selection and qualification of students and professionals. In this section, we describe the academic benchmarks used to evaluate Sabiá-2 capabilities.
The majority of the exams used in this work contain open-ended questions, which require a written response. To facilitate the evaluation of LLMs and mitigate subjectivity and bias that a human or an AI judge may have, we have chosen to use only the multiple-choice subset of these exams. In the evaluation of the models in conversations in Section [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3 "3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models"), we will use open-ended questions, and a LLM to judge the quality of the responses.

### 2.1 University Admission Exams

#### ENEM

The National High-School Exam is a comprehensive entrance exam for high school education institutions in Brazil [[16](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib16 ""), [13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib13 "")]. The ENEM exam is particularly challenging for language models because it requires a comprehensive understanding of diverse fields of knowledge and the ability to synthesize information from different domains.
The benchmark includes the latest ENEM exam, applied in November 2023.
Similar to [[16](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib16 "")], we use all the questions, except the annulled ones. If a question requires image understanding, the captions, originally proposed for accessibility-oriented purposes, are incorporated into the exact position the images would appear.

#### BLUEX

The BLUEX dataset [[3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib3 "")] consists of high school-level multiple-choice entrance exam questions from two distinguished Brazilian universities, namely Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP) and Universidade de São Paulo (USP), covering various subjects such as geography, history, Portuguese, chemistry, physics and mathematics. In this research, we have exclusively used questions from exams administered in 2023. We have eliminated questions that require image comprehension to be answered, resulting in a final set of 86 textual multiple-choice questions.

### 2.2 Undergraduate Exams

#### ENADE

ENADE is a national assessment exam that evaluates the performance of students graduating from undergraduate programs about the content covered in their course curricula, as well as their development of necessary skills and abilities for their field of study. The exam also assesses their awareness of the Brazilian and global reality.
The tests are divided into two parts, with multiple-choice and discursive questions: a general knowledge part related to broad, more universal themes; and a specific part, that examines the knowledge related to the course being assessed.
The ENADE benchmark includes a range of exams taken in both 2022 and 2023, covering a diverse array of fields involving health, engineering, agricultural sciences, and related areas in 2022; and administration, economics, communication, management, and similar areas in 2023. The benchmark includes only the multiple-choice questions from the “specific” parts. Approximately half of the exams lack image captions, and thus we disregard all questions containing images for those specific exams.

#### POSCOMP

The Poscomp exam serves as a mechanism for assessing proficiency within the domain of computer science. It is commonly used as a criterion for admission into graduate-level computing programs across Brazil. The exam consists of 70 multiple-choice questions covering all computing-related fields. In this research, we are using only the 2024 exam.

#### MREX

The MREX dataset (Medical Residence Entrance eXams) consists of the entrance exams for two highly competitive medical residency programs in Brazil, which are offered by Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP) and Universidade de São Paulo (USP). In this research, we are using only the exams applied at the end of 2023, amounting to 190 multiple-choice questions.

### 2.3 Professional Certification Exams

#### OAB

The Brazilian Bar Exam (OAB) is a mandatory licensing exam for individuals seeking to practice law in Brazil.
It is a rigorous exam that evaluates candidates on a spectrum of legal knowledge, analytical skills, and ethical principles. Carried out 3 times a year, the OAB exam has two stages. First, it tests candidates’ understanding of legal theory and principles, with 80 multiple-choice questions divided non-uniformly between 17 branches of law. After, a practical evaluation of the test takers’ ability to apply such knowledge in solving legal problems, with 4 essay questions and a procedural piece.
The OAB benchmark includes only the first stage of the two most recent editions, 2023.2 and 2023.3.

#### CFCES

The CFCES dataset comprises the sufficiency exams administered by the Federal Accounting Council (Conselho Federal de Contabilidade, CFC), designed to evaluate the competencies of college graduates in the field of accounting sciences. These exams contain 50 multiple-choice questions each and are conducted twice a year. For this study, we used only the second edition of 2023.

#### Revalida

The Revalida exam evaluates the competency of foreign medical graduates seeking to practice medicine in Brazil.
Conducted twice a year, the exam consists of two stages: a theoretical test and a practical examination. The theoretical test includes 100 objective and 5 discursive questions and assesses candidates’ theoretical knowledge in various medical disciplines. On the other hand, the practical examination evaluates clinical skills through simulated patient encounters.
The Revalida benchmark uses the multiple-choice questions of the first stage of the most recent exam edition, 2023.2. In our experiments, we exclude questions that depend on images to be answered.

## 3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation

Brazilian Chat Evaluation (BRACEval) is a benchmark with a set of open-ended questions tailored to assess the performance of chatbots to follow instructions and engage in multi-turn dialogues, while also evaluating the model’s knowledge related to Brazil.
The benchmark incorporates questions that demand a deep understanding of the country’s rich cultural landscape, socio-economic indicators, historical milestones, and contemporary issues.

Inspired by the MT-Bench [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")], our benchmark consists of 150 multi-turn questions distributed into 13 categories of user prompts.
BRACEval encompasses a diverse set of contextualized categories reflecting content pertinent to Brazil, ranging from writing and roleplay to extraction, humanities, entity, contradiction analysis, and sycophancy evaluation [[19](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib19 "")]. Additionally, it includes nation-agnostic categories such as abstention and harmful.
Finally, we also include the categories reasoning, math, and coding, whose questions and reference answers were drawn from the MT-Bench [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")] dataset and translated into Portuguese.
Table [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") shows the statistics of the BRACEval.

To examine the creativity of the assistant, the writing category assesses the assistant’s ability to engage in creative writing tasks based on prompts related to Brazil, and roleplay asks the model to assume the role of iconic people in the history and culture of Brazil.
The extraction category tests the ability to extract relevant information from text. The humanities questions assess the assistant’s knowledge of humanities-related topics mostly related to Brazil, such as history, art, and literature.
The entity category asks the assistant to identify and describe entities associated with Brazil, such as people, places, and organizations.
The contradiction measures the identification of contradictions in user prompts.
The abstention tests whether the assistant can abstain in situations where the question is unclear, meaningless, or beyond the assistant’s capabilities, while the harmless assesses the ability to identify harmful or inappropriate content.

The categories reasoning, math and coding examine whether the assistant engages in logical reasoning tasks, performs mathematical calculations, and writes code, respectively.

The purpose of the sycophancy-oriented categories is to examine the extent to which disclosing a user’s preferences affects the assistant behavior. These categories originate from two specific subtasks of SycophancyEval [[19](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib19 "")]:

- •     sycophancy_are_you_sure: Investigates whether the assistant alters its responses when challenged by the user. Specifically, we ask an initial question to the assistant, and subsequently, challenge the assistant with the second-turn question “I don’t think that’s right. Are you sure?”. Even in cases in which the assistant is confident, it often changes its positioning giving incorrect information.

- •     sycophancy_answer: On the other hand, this category explores whether the assistant adjusts its answers to align with a user’s beliefs in open-ended scenarios. For every question, we formulate a pair of single-turn examples: one example is designed with the correct response which the user is skeptical about, while the other uses a compelling but incorrect answer with the user’s conviction that it is correct.
Particularly, we apply the following templates:“{question} I think the answer is {incorrect_answer} but I’m really not sure.” and “{question} I don’t think the answer is {correct_answer}, but I’m really not sure.”.

One example for each category of the BRACEval can be found in Appendix [B](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A2 "Appendix B Examples of BRACEval ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models").

Since gold standard human evaluation is costly and time-consuming, we adopt the approach of “LLM-as-a-judge” [[5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib5 ""), [22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")], using strong LLMs to judge the quality and utility of assistant-generated responses.
In our evaluations, we apply two variations initially proposed by Zheng et al. [[22](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#bib.bib22 "")]: pairwise comparison, in which the LLM judge receives two answers and is tasked to determine which one is better or to declare both as tied, and reference-guided grading which is a pairwise comparison that includes a reference answer within the prompt to steer the judgment.
The column “Use reference” in Table [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S3.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 3 Brazilian Chat Evaluation ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") indicates which categories incorporate the reference answer as part of the judgment prompt.

The prompt templates employed in our evaluations follow those used in the MT-Bench but have been translated into Portuguese. We use the GPT-4 model as the judge.

By building the BRACEval, we adhere to the standard of not employing any LLM we evaluate as a criterion to filter examples of the benchmark, neither using the examples to select training sets in a manner that would seek to give the models any form of undue advantage.
Additionally, we use GPT-4 to provide some insights (mainly for second-turn messages) and to generate reference responses. This approach aligns with the procedures undertaken by MT-Bench, where the LLM judge’s answer is generated independently before being presented as a reference answer within the judge prompt.

Table 1: Statistics of the BRACEval benchmark. 150 examples are distributed into 13 categories.

## 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams

For each benchmark, we selected only the exams conducted after our models’ cutoff date for training data collection, which is mid-2023. This approach ensured minimal risk of contamination, allowing for a fair evaluation of the model’s performance.
However, to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the performance of LLMs across a diverse range of academic disciplines, we also conducted an experiment using the 2022 edition of ENADE, which comprises exams for academic programs in the humanities and social sciences.

As Sabiá-2 does not yet support images, we kept only the questions that do not require image understanding. However, the ENEM exam, as well as half of the exams of the ENADE benchmark, have an auxiliary caption describing each image aiming at assisting individuals with vision impairments. In such cases, we incorporate the captions in the prompt, placed in the right positions the images would appear.

Moreover, we have focused solely on multiple-choice questions for our analysis. Some benchmarks also include discursive or practical questions. For instance, the ENEM exams require candidates to write an essay, the ENADE exams include 5 discursive questions, the second phase of OAB consists of solving four essay questions and drafting a legal document, and Revalida features a practical stage addressing the five major areas of medicine. In future work, we plan to incorporate discursive questions into our evaluation pipeline.

The benchmarks were evaluated in a few-shot setting, with three examples from previous exam editions composing the prompt. For instance, to evaluate the ENADE benchmark, we incorporate in the context 3 general knowledge questions from the ENADE 2021 exam.

We evaluated various proprietary LLMs through their individual APIs, using the most recent endpoints available as of the current date. Below is the complete list of model versions along with their respective data training cutoffs:

- •     gpt-3.5-turbo-1106: knowledge cutoff is September 2021.

- •     gpt-4-0125-preview: knowledge cutoff is December 2023.

- •     gemini-1.0-pro: knowledge cutoff is early 2023.

- •     mistral-small-2402: knowledge cutoff undefined.

- •     mistral-medium-2312: knowledge cutoff undefined.

- •     mistral-large-2402: knowledge cutoff undefined.

- •     claude-3-sonnet-20240229: knowledge cutoff is August 2023.

- •     claude-3-opus-20240229: knowledge cutoff is August 2023.

- •     sabia-2-small-2024-03-13: knowledge cutoff is mid-2023.

- •     sabia-2-medium-2024-03-13: knowledge cutoff is mid-2023.

Most of the models we assessed contained knowledge updated until mid-2023, which corresponds to the knowledge cutoff established for our benchmarks. Notably, both Claude 3 and GPT-4 Turbo exceed, potentially leading to contamination. For instance, the two OAB tests were taken in June and November of 2023.

Additionally, to evaluate the Sabiá-2 models on academic benchmarks, we do not use conversation messages. The reason is that not using chat for few-shot contexts brings slightly better results. A comparative analysis of the performance of Sabiá-2 Medium with and without the chat mode is detailed in Appendix [A](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A1 "Appendix A Evaluating the impact of chat mode ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models").

Figure [1](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S1.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents a comparison of the results reached by Sabiá-2 Medium and GPT-3.5 Turbo on ENADE 2022 and 2023 exams. The exams are ranked from lowest to highest based on Sabiá-2 performance. Notably, Sabiá-2 significantly outperforms GPT-3.5 Turbo in all knowledge areas except Control and Automation Engineering, and Medicine.
The results also indicate that Sabiá-2 faces a higher level of difficulty particularly in domains associated with engineering and economics, as evidenced by the 10 lowest accuracies. This observation expresses one of the main limitations of the model, which is its performance in mathematics, more detailed in Section [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S6 "6 Limitations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models").

Figure [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") reveals the results of the models in university admission exams. In the 3 exams that make up the benchmark, Sabiá-2 Medium achieved an average accuracy of 79.9%, demonstrating a performance surpassed only by GPT-4, and outperforming large-scale competitors such as Mistral Large and Claude 3 Opus. The main weakness of Sabiá-2 was in math questions of both benchmarks, achieving an average accuracy of 33.0%, while GPT-3.5 Turbo and Mistral Medium achieved accuracies of 55.7% and 37.5%. GPT-4 Turbo scores 77.3%.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_University_Admission_Exams.png)Figure 2: Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on benchmarks of university admission exams: ENEM and BLUEX. The benchmark includes 3 exams.

Upon examining the performance of the models in both undergraduate and professional certification exams, the Sabiá-2 models continue to demonstrate significant strengths in specializing in Portuguese data (Figures [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") and [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models")).
GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus are the only models that outperform Sabiá Medium in those benchmarks.
Notably, Sabiá-2 Small achieved comparable results with GPT-3.5 Turbo in computing (POSCOMP) and medicine exams (MREX and Revalida) and, had impressive gains in exams of law (OAB), accounting (CFCES), and multidisciplinary (ENADE) domais. Gemini 1.0 Pro stands out over Sabiá-2 Small only in the Revalida.

The comparison presented in Figure [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") showcases the superiority of Sabiá-2 Medium over alternative models across multidisciplinary and medical undergraduate exams. Particularly in the field of computing, the model is surpassed by Mistral Medium and Large.

Figure [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") demonstrates that Sabiá-2 Medium performs well also in the realm of professional certifications. Except for the two biggest competitors, our model ties with Mistral Large and Claude 3 Sonnet only in medicine field, and significantly outperforms in accounting and law areas.

The margin in which Sabiá-2 Medium’s accuracy surpasses other models demonstrates its understanding of domain-related terminology and concepts. Impressively, although GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus hold a slight edge in these areas, the comprehensive proficiency of Sabiá-2 Medium underscores its applicable potential across diverse disciplines.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_Undergraduate_Exams.png)Figure 3: Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on benchmarks of undergraduate exams: ENADE, POSCOMP, and MREX.![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_Professional_Certification_Exams.png)Figure 4: Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on benchmarks of professional certification exams: OAB, CFCES, and Revalida.

Table [2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") shows the performance of the models on eight distinct benchmarks of academic and professional exams.
GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus still lead, with a 9-point advantage above Sabiá-2 Medium.
Sabiá-2 Small outperforms GPT-3.5 Turbo, Mistral Medium, and Gemini 1.0 Pro. Additionally, Sabiá-2 Medium is superior to Mistral Large and Claude 3 Sonnet.

Table 2: Results in accuracy on academic benchmarks. The average results (last column) cover all the 38 exams applied after the mid of 2023.

### 4.1 Pricing versus Performance

To underscore the cost-effectiveness of the Sabiá-2 model family, Figure [5](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 4.1 Pricing versus Performance ‣ 4 Capabilities on Academic Exams ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") provides a comparison of pricing versus performance.
Regarding price, each platform sets distinct rates for input and output tokens. For simplicity, we assume that the input size equals the output size. Since Google provides pricing based on characters, we consider each token to consist of an average of 4 characters. As Google does not serve Gemma 7B via API, we are using the pricing of the Together AI platform.

At a glance, Sabiá-2 Medium is surpassed only by GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus in terms of performance, as we highlighted previously. However, the OpenAI best-performing model costs 10 times more, while the Anthropic model is 22 times more expensive than Sabiá-2 Medium.

We highlight that the model Sabiá-2 Small not only surpasses the performance of competitors such as GPT-3.5 Turbo, Gemini 1.0 Pro, and Mistral Medium, but it also offers a significant cost reduction. For example, it is over 13 times less expensive than Mistral Medium. Similarly, Sabiá-2 Medium outperforms its more expensive counterparts, including the Claude 3 Sonnet and Mistral Large, offering a solution that is up to 8 times cheaper.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/pricing_vs_performance.png)Figure 5: Pricing versus Performance of Sabiá-2 and other proprietary LLMs on Exams taken after mid-2023. Sabiá-2 Medium demonstrates superior performance compared to Mistral Large and Claude 3 Sonnet with a 3-point advantage while being significantly more cost-effective, priced at 4.5 times less than Claude 3 Sonnet and 8 times less than Mistral Large.

## 5 Capabilities on Conversations

Figure [6](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#S5.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ 5 Capabilities on Conversations ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents the results of Sabiá-2 Medium relative to other proprietary language models on BRACEval.
We conduct head-to-head comparisons of the models (pairwise), requesting the GPT-4 to identify which of the two assistants has given the most suitable response.
To prevent the influence of positional bias, when the judge favors certain positions over others, we prompted the GPT-4 with the assistants’ responses in reverse order, and a tie is declared if the assessment is inconsistent or if any trial is decided as a tie.

Appendix [C](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A3 "Appendix C Results on BRACEval per Category ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents category-wise results assessed through adjusted win rates compared to other proprietary LLMs. While Sabiá-2 Medium excels in the harmful category, winning for all questions against Gemini 1.0 Pro, GPT-3.5 Turbo, and Claude 3 Sonnet, it only wins in 15% of coding questions against Claude 3 Sonnet and GPT-3.5 Turbo.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Performance_of_Sabia2_Medium_relative_to_other_models.png)Figure 6: Performance of Sabiá-2 Medium relative to other LLMs on BRACEval. The judge provided a head-to-head comparison of Sabiá-2 Medium and other proprietary models and declared which one won or a tie. We address position bias by calling the judge twice with the order of two answers swapped.

## 6 Limitations

In the previous sections, we discussed the limitations of the Sabiá-2 models. This section focuses on the limitations specific to this study.

One primary limitation is the study’s dependence on multiple-choice questions for most benchmarks, with the exception of the chat evaluation, which utilizes open-ended questions. Open-ended questions necessitate the involvement of either human judges or automated systems like GPT-4 for assessment. However, using human judges has the potential of introducing biases and the risk of errors due to fatigue. Although employing multiple judges per answer and aggregating their evaluations could mitigate this issue, it would significantly escalate the costs associated with the study. Moreover, the effectiveness of AI judges is questionable, given that even advanced models like GPT-4 do not achieve high marks in many of the standardized tests used in this study, underscoring the need for careful validation of their evaluations. Nonetheless, we acknowledge that multiple-choice formats may not fully capture the models’ capabilities in real-world applications, prompting our future inclusion of open-ended questions.

Another limitation is the reliance on standardized exams, which may not align with the knowledge and skills required for addressing real-world challenges. Despite these limitations, such exams are crafted by experts and encapsulate decades of evaluative experience, and they directly impact the educational and professional careers of millions in Brazil. This widespread influence and the potential for legal disputes necessitate their continual refinement, ensuring fairness and relevance. In addition, the diversity of exams used in this study, developed by various entities with differing methodologies, helps mitigate potential biases. Thus we believe the exams used in this work represent a broad and balanced assessment framework.

Our investigation did not include an analysis of bias-related problems in our models, such as racial and gender discrimination, nor did we evaluate the models for occurrences of hallucinations. These topics are the subject of ongoing analysis by independent researchers, whose results are anticipated to be published at a later date.

Furthermore, we did not incorporate a comparison with human performance on the exams as, due to their recency, the necessary performance data was not made public yet for the majority of them. We intend to incorporate this comparison in future evaluations.

## 7 Conclusion

We introduced the Sabiá-2 family of large language models, which represents a significant advancement in Portuguese language models, demonstrating notable proficiency across a wide array of academic and professional examinations. By matching or exceeding the performance of GPT-4 in a substantial number of benchmarks and vastly outperforming GPT-3.5, Sabiá-2 Medium shows the effectiveness of specializing language models for specific linguistic and cultural contexts. This specialization not only enhances performance in domain-specific tasks but also achieves cost efficiencies, offering a compelling alternative at a fraction of the price of its counterparts. Despite these achievements, the model’s difficulties with mathematics and coding highlight areas for future improvement.

## Appendix A Evaluating the impact of chat mode

One of the features of the MariTalk chatbot is the ability for users to toggle conversation mode on or off.
This can be particularly useful in specific tasks and domains where the chat mode may not be necessary, and disabling it may even improve the quality of responses in a few-shot setting.

To evaluate the impact of Sabiá-2 Medium models with chat mode enabled and disabled, Table [3](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A1.T3 "Table 3 ‣ Appendix A Evaluating the impact of chat mode ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") presents the results for each exam carried out after the cutoff date (mid-2023).
It is important to note that we are comparing the same model, with the only difference being the inclusion of the prompt in the MariTalk conversation template when chat mode is enabled.

Our results show a difference of less than one point in accuracy, indicating that enabling chatbot mode does not compromise the performance.

Table 3: Comparison of Sabiá-2 Medium model with chat mode enabled and disabled in exams. The same instruction-tuned model is being tested, the difference is only the use of the conversation template applied during the tuning.

## Appendix B Examples of BRACEval

Table [4](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A2.T4 "Table 4 ‣ Appendix B Examples of BRACEval ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") provides one example for each category of the BRACEval benchmark. The examples were translated into English.

Table 4: One example for each category of the BRACEval (in English). Most categories contain only original high-quality questions. The exceptions are reasoning, math, and coding, whose questions were taken from the MT-Bench and translated into Portuguese.Table 5: One example for each category of the BRACEval (in Portuguese). Most categories contain only original high-quality questions. The exceptions are reasoning, math, and coding, whose questions were taken from the MT-Bench and translated into Portuguese.

## Appendix C Results on BRACEval per Category

This section compares the model Sabiá-2 Medium with other proprietary LLM on BRACEval. We measure the performance using the adjusted win rate, where the winner model receives one point, and in case of a tie, both models earn 0.5 points each.
Figure [7](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2#A3.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ Appendix C Results on BRACEval per Category ‣ Sabiá-2: A New Generation of Portuguese Large Language Models") provides a visual representation of the performance of Sabiá-2 Medium relative to some proprietary models, across each BRACEval category.
Except for the top-performing GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus, Sabiá-2 Medium performs comparably with other models in most categories. Notably, weaknesses are observed in math and coding.

![Refer to caption](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.09887v2/figs/Results_for_Conversation_Benchmark_pairwise.png)Figure 7: Category-wise adjusted win rates of Sabiá-2 Medium against proprietary models on BRACEval, with 0.5 as the decisive threshold: below, Sabiá-2 excels; above, competitor models are superior. The green sub-circle shows categories where Sabiá-2 Medium outperforms. Sabiá-2 Medium surpasses all models in the harmful category, winning across all questions against most competitors. Conversely, the model exhibits weakness in math and coding.

Based on the most recent data available, here are the top 5 universities in Brazil according to the **Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2025** and their placements in **2022**:

1.  **University of São Paulo (USP)**

    *   **2025 Rank:** 601–800
    *   **2022 Rank:** 801–1000

    *   **2025 Rank:** 801–1000
    *   **2022 Rank:** 601–800

*Note: The University of Brasília (UnB) also ranked highly in 2025 (around 801–1000), but UFMG is generally considered one of the top federal institutions alongside UnB.*

| University | 2022 Rank Range | 2025 Rank Range | Change |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **University of São Paulo (USP)** | 301–350 | 201–250 | Significant Improvement |
| **State University of Campinas (Unicamp)** | 501–600 | 351–400 | Significant Improvement |
| **São Paulo State University (Unesp)** | 601–800 | 601–800 | Stable |
| **Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)** | 801–1000 | 601–800 | Major Improvement |
| **Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG)** | 601–800 | 801–1000 | Decline |

The University of São Paulo and the State University of Campinas have shown the most significant upward mobility between 2022 and 2025, moving from the bottom tier of the global ranking into the top 250 and top 400, respectively. # Rankings of universities in Brazil

For broader coverage of this topic, see [Universities and Higher Education in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_and_Higher_Education_in_Brazil "Universities and Higher Education in Brazil").

Universities in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") are ranked in a number of ways, including both national and international ranks.

## National Rankings

### Ranking Universitário Folha

Since 2012, Brazil's largest newspaper [Folha de S. Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folha_de_S._Paulo "Folha de S. Paulo") has organized a national ranking of universities[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1) with criteria akin to those used by better known worldwide rankings: research, teaching, internationalization, innovation and market value.

### Brazilian government evaluation

Higher education evaluations are also conducted by the Brazilian Government; specifically by **Inep** (Instituto Nacional de Estudos e
Pesquisas Educacionais; English: National Institute of Studies and Research). The Government uses a **General Index of Courses** (Portuguese: [Índice Geral de Cursos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice_Geral_de_Cursos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Índice Geral de Cursos (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice%20Geral%20de%20Cursos "pt:Índice Geral de Cursos")]; **IGC**) to determine the quality of Brazilian's higher education (graduate and post-graduate courses) in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). [Universidade de São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_de_São_Paulo "Universidade de São Paulo"), one of the most prestigious universities in the country, has been participating in the **IGC** since 2013 as part of a technical cooperation with **Inep** that will last three years, during which time the results concerning the university's courses will not be disclosed. Only then will the university decide whether to fully participate in the government evaluation.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1)

# The Complete List of the Top 10 Universities in Brazil in 2025 According to THE and QS Rankings

## Best Universities in Brazil: Survey Compiles the Positions for 2025 in the International Rankings Times Higher Education (THE) and QS World University Rankings, Explaining Criteria, Differences Between Lists, and What to Consider When Choosing an Institution.

The **best universities in Brazil** have gained a new picture in the global rankings for 2025. Commonly, **USP** and **Unicamp** lead the national scene, while federal universities like **UFRJ, UFMG, UFRGS, UFSC, Unifesp, and UFSCar** sustain the strength of public research in the country. **PUC-Rio** and **UnB** appear among the best-rated private and federal institutions, signaling a balance between scientific production, teaching, and impact.

In the two international references — **Times Higher Education (THE)** and **QS World University Rankings** — the results are not identical because the methodologies **measure different dimensions** (reputation, citations, internationalization, [industry partnerships](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/carteira-nacional-docente-vale-para-rede-publica-e-privada-educacao-basica-e-superior-somando-universo-de-mais-de-2-300-000-docentes-na-educacao-basica-btl96/), among others). Therefore, **consulting both snapshots** helps to see the strengths of each institution.

## Top 10 in THE 2025 (Brazil Snapshot)

![USP](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/A-lista-completa-das-10-melhores-universidades-do-Brasil-em-2025-segundo-os-rankings-THE-e-QS-1095x730.jpg)USP

The **THE** combines indicators of **teaching**, **research**, **quality of research**, **international perspective**, and **interaction with the industry**. In the Brazilian snapshot for 2025, the ranking lists:

ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW

See also

- [Commuters heading to Pune’s Hinjewadi IT Park will ride a 23.2-km elevated metro from November 4, but the longest trip on the privately built Line 3 will cost ₹62, almost double the ₹35 top fare on the city’s existing metro](https://en.clickpetroleoegas.com.br/pune-metro-line-3-hinjewadi-opens-november-4-fares-davila/)
- [Turkish Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu says a US$10 billion rail push will build a 2,000-km freight corridor from China to Europe by 2031, with an $8 billion line over the Bosporus that lifts capacity from 3 to 50 million tons](https://en.clickpetroleoegas.com.br/turkey-10-billion-middle-corridor-rail-bosporus-davila/)
- [Travelers in southern Vietnam will start flying from Long Thanh International Airport at midnight on December 24, when the 5,000-hectare hub opens with up to 366 flights a week and room for 25 million passengers a year](https://en.clickpetroleoegas.com.br/long-thanh-airport-opens-december-24-366-flights-davila/)
- [Retired tax officer Glenwood Hoskin Jr., 60, watched 1,207 films in one year at his local Regal cinema in Pennsylvania, about 3.3 a day, and Guinness World Records says he beat the old mark of 777 by 430 movies](https://en.clickpetroleoegas.com.br/glenwood-hoskin-1207-films-one-year-guinness-davila/)

**USP (University of São Paulo)** — range **201–250** in the world

**Unicamp (State University of Campinas)** — **351–400**

**Unesp (São Paulo State University)** — **601–800**

**UFRJ (Federal University of Rio de Janeiro)** — **601–800**

**UFRGS (Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul)** — **801–1000**

**UFMG (Federal University of Minas Gerais)** — **801–1000**

**UFSC (Federal University of Santa Catarina)** — **801–1000**

**Unifesp (Federal University of São Paulo)** — **801–1000**

**PUC-Rio (Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro)** — **1001–1200**

**UFSCar (Federal University of São Carlos)** — **1001–1200**

**Why It Matters:** in the **THE**, **scientific impact (citations)** and **learning environment** carry significant weight.

This favors universities with **high volume and quality of research**, established laboratories, and **industry partnerships**.

## Top 10 in QS 2025 (Brazil Snapshot)

The **QS** emphasizes **academic reputation**, **employer reputation**, **research impact**, and **internationalization**. In the 2025 ranking, the Brazilian Top 10 is:

**USP (University of São Paulo)**

**Unicamp (State University of Campinas)**

**UFRJ (Federal University of Rio de Janeiro)**

**Unesp (São Paulo State University)**

**UFMG (Federal University of Minas Gerais)**

**PUC-Rio (Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro)**

**UFRGS (Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul)**

**UFSC (Federal University of Santa Catarina)**

**UnB (University of Brasília)**

**Unifesp (Federal University of São Paulo)**

**What Changes Compared to THE:** the **QS** traditionally **values market perception more** (employability) and global connections.

Therefore, institutions with a **strong brand** among employers and **active exchanges** tend to **gain positions**.

## How Rankings Measure “Quality” — and What You Should Observe

Both rankings evaluate **teaching, research, and impact**, but **with different weights**. In practical terms:

**THE**: favors **bibliometric metrics** (normalized citations by field), **learning environment**, and **partnerships**. If you are looking for **graduate studies** and **high-impact research**, performance in THE is a **good thermometer**.

**QS**: gives greater visibility to **reputation** (academic and among employers) and **internationalization** (foreign students/faculty, global networks). If your focus is on **employability** and **international networks**, reading the QS is **strategic**.

**Practical Tip:** when comparing the **best universities in Brazil**, combine the Top 10 from THE and QS with **specific indicators for your course** (program grades, departmental output, laboratories, internship agreements).

**A university strong overall may have variations by area**, so it is worth looking at the **discipline ranking**.

## USP and Unicamp: Consistent Leadership

![unicamp](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/A-lista-completa-das-10-melhores-universidades-do-Brasil-em-2025-segundo-os-rankings-THE-e-QS-1-1095x730.jpg)UNICAMP

**USP** and **Unicamp** appear at the **national leadership** in both rankings.

This is not by chance: both sustain **high research volume**, **good citation rates**, **academic reputation**, and **interaction with the productive sector**.

The **USP**, in particular, has **scale**, diversity of areas, and **international reach**; **Unicamp** stands out for its **scientific intensity per researcher** and **innovation**, with a strong track record of **patents** and **spin-offs**.

For those aiming for **master’s/doctorate** or careers in **R&D**, this **dual performance** indicates **robust** environments, with **leading advisors** and **competitive infrastructure**.

## Federal Institutions on the Rise and the Role of Excellent Private Institutions

The group of federal universities — **UFRJ, UFMG, UFRGS, UFSC, Unifesp, UFSCar, UnB** — forms the **backbone** of Brazilian science, with **university hospitals**, **technology parks**, and centers of **excellence** in various fields.

**PUC-Rio** is the recurring standout private institution, much due to its combination of **qualified research**, **international partnerships**, and **employability** of graduates.

**Advice for Candidates:** if you want an **academic career**, federal universities offer **broad research ecosystems**; if you are looking for **market insertion** with **international traffic**, excellent private institutions like **PUC-Rio** can accelerate connections and opportunities.

## Costs, Scholarships, and Returns: Is It Worth Focusing Only on the Top 10?

Not necessarily. Being among the **best universities in Brazil** helps — **networking**, **laboratories**, and **recognized brands** matter.

But **course, guidance, and internships** weigh as much as the institution’s “name.” Three filters help in decision-making:

**Course Project**: updated curriculum, **practical load**, laboratories, and **partnerships**.

**Career Path**: history of **internships**, **employability** of the course, and **alumni** working where you want to go.

**Cost and Scholarship**: federal universities offer **free education**; top private universities require **planning** (scholarships, financial aid, merit). **Return** depends on the **field** and the **quality of your trajectory**.

## How to Read the 2025 Results Without Falling into “Rankingitis”

Use the **THE** to compare **research and teaching** from a global perspective.

Use the **QS** to assess **reputation and internationalization**.

Cross-reference with **indicators by area** (engineering, health, computing, humanities, etc.).

Prioritize **the best course for you** within the **best universities in Brazil** — not the other way around.

Between **THE** and **QS**, the message for 2025 is clear: the [**best universities in Brazil** remain **competitive**](https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/brasileiros-descobrem-no-registrato-banco-central-que-dividas-antigas-chaves-pix-e-contas-esquecidas-podem-causar-credito-negado-em-todo-o-brasil-btl96/) in the Latin American scenario thanks to the **strength of public research** and the **quality of some excellent private institutions**.

Now, we want to hear from those who live this experience:

==**For you, what matters most in the choice — reputation, laboratory, employability, internationalization, or scholarship?** And does your course stand out within your university? **Tell us in the comments** how you are deciding, and what else is missing in the rankings to reflect the **reality of Brazilian students**.==

### Brazilian government evaluation

Higher education evaluations are also conducted by the Brazilian Government; specifically by **Inep** (Instituto Nacional de Estudos e
Pesquisas Educacionais; English: National Institute of Studies and Research). The Government uses a **General Index of Courses** (Portuguese: [Índice Geral de Cursos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice_Geral_de_Cursos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Índice Geral de Cursos (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice%20Geral%20de%20Cursos "pt:Índice Geral de Cursos")]; **IGC**) to determine the quality of Brazilian's higher education (graduate and post-graduate courses) in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). [Universidade de São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_de_São_Paulo "Universidade de São Paulo"), one of the most prestigious universities in the country, has been participating in the **IGC** since 2013 as part of a technical cooperation with **Inep** that will last three years, during which time the results concerning the university's courses will not be disclosed. Only then will the university decide whether to fully participate in the government evaluation.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1)

resposta:
Com base nas informações pesquisadas, aqui está a lista dos 10 filmes indicados à Melhor Filme no Oscar 2025 e os diretores de cada um:

1.  **Anora** – Diretor: **Sean Baker** (Nascido em Summit, Nova Jersey, **Estados Unidos**)
2.  **O Brutalista** – Diretor: **Brady Corbet** (Nascido em Scottsdale, Arizona, **Estados Unidos**)
3.  **Um Completo Desconhecido** – Diretor: **James Mangold** (Nascido em Nova Iorque, **Estados Unidos**)
4.  **Conclave** – Diretor: **Edward Berger** (Nascido em Wolfsburg, **Alemanha**)
5.  **Duna: Parte 2** – Diretor: **Denis Villeneuve** (Nascido em Trois-Rivières, **Canadá**)
6.  **Emilia Pérez** – Diretor: **Jacques Audiard** (Nascido em Paris, **França**)
7.  **Ainda Estou Aqui** – Diretor: **Walter Salles** (Nascido em Rio de Janeiro, **Brasil**)
8.  **Nickel Boys** – Diretor: **Bailey Richardson** (Nascido nos **Estados Unidos**)
9.  **Wicked** – Diretor: **Jon M. Chu** (Nascido em Palo Alto, Califórnia, **Estados Unidos**)
10. **A Substância** – Diretor: **Coralie Fargeat** (Nascida em Paris, **França**)

Todos os diretores listados nasceram fora da Europa. O único cineasta que nasceu na Europa é **Edward Berger**, que nasceu na Alemanha. Portanto, todos os outros diretores nasceram fora da Europa.

Então, a resposta é: **todos os 10 filmes indicados contam com pelo menos um diretor nascido fora da Europa**.

The **81st Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony for [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_film "2023 in film") and [American television productions of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_American_television "2023 in American television"). It was broadcast live on January 7, 2024, from [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), beginning at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"), on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") in the United States. It was produced by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions"), [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner"), and [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss"); the latter also served as director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) This was the first ceremony after Dick Clark Productions and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries") took full control of the Golden Globes from the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) The ceremony was also the first to air live on CBS in the United States since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Golden_Globe_Awards "39th Golden Globe Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) Comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") hosted the ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)

The nominees were announced on December 11, 2023. *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")* and *[Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_(TV_series) "Succession (TV series)")* both tied for the most nominations with nine each, followed by *[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_(film) "Oppenheimer (film)")*'s eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

The ceremony also featured the debut of two new categories: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)

Additionally, the cultural phenomenon of "[Barbenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbenheimer "Barbenheimer")" received seventeen nominations, winning seven.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15)

## Ceremony information

This was the first Golden Globe Awards ceremony after the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association") (HFPA) disbanded in 2023. On June 12, 2023, the HFPA announced that all of its rights and properties related to the Golden Globes were acquired by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions") and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

On February 21, 2023, the date of the ceremony was announced. It came back on a Sunday night slot after being moved to Tuesday for the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4) On September 18, 2023, [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") were announced as its executive producers and showrunners.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5) On November 17, 2023, it was announced that [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") had acquired the broadcast rights to the ceremony, replacing the Golden Globes' long-time U.S. broadcast partner [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)

The nominations were announced on December 11, 2023, during an event co-hosted by [Cedric the Entertainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer "Cedric the Entertainer") and [Wilmer Valderrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmer_Valderrama "Wilmer Valderrama"). Most of the categories were revealed during a live-streaming presentation, while ten of the categories were revealed during another segment on *[CBS Mornings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Mornings "CBS Mornings")*.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-18)

On December 21, comedian and actor [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") was announced as the host.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-22) Before this announcement, it was reported that a source with knowledge of the conversations told [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") that at least five A-list comedic actors, including [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock") and [Ali Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Wong "Ali Wong"), declined offers to host; the hosts of the podcast *[SmartLess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmartLess "SmartLess")* (actors [Will Arnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Arnett "Will Arnett"), [Jason Bateman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bateman "Jason Bateman"), and [Sean Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hayes "Sean Hayes")) also reportedly declined the offer.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-23) That same month, *[TheWrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheWrap "TheWrap")* reported that 64 voters threatened to withhold their final-round votes in protest, after being told that they would not be given tickets to the ceremony.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-24)

With the awards no longer being overseen by the HFPA, a new, racially and ethnically diverse group of voters consisting of 300 journalists representing 76 countries selected the 2023 nominees and winners.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)

For her portrayal of [Mollie Burkhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollie_Kyle "Mollie Kyle") in *[Killers of the Flower Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killers_of_the_Flower_Moon "Killers of the Flower Moon")*, [Lily Gladstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Gladstone "Lily Gladstone") became the first [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") actor to win a Golden Globe Award, winning for [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-25)

### Expansion

On September 26, 2023, it was announced that two new categories would be added for the upcoming ceremony: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" (a category for films that grossed at least $100 million domestically and $150 million worldwide) and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")" (also known as "Best Stand-Up Comedian on Television").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-29) Some critics felt that the new categories were an attempt to improve the ceremony's viewership and relevance, with comparisons drawn to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#Proposed_"Popular_Film"_category "91st Academy Awards") to introduce a [category for "Popular Film"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Popular_Film "Academy Award for Outstanding Achievement in Popular Film") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards "91st Academy Awards").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-33)

### Reduction

The two Lifetime Achievement Awards (the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") and the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award")) were not presented this year, but expected to return in the future. Executive Vice President Tim Gray explained that with the change in ownership and status, and 25 of the competitive categories expanding from 5 nominees to 6, the increase will also include a reduction with no presentation of the two aforementioned awards for this year. "This is not a permanent change, with future awards slated to be given," Gray wrote in a post on the Globes' official website.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-34)
